card.name: Punctuation after regulatory REMS clauses
card.fires_on: The comma or next small word right after an introductory clause about FDA requirements, REMS, or unproven uses. It marks the spot where a regulator or rule-setter is about to come up as the subject.

modes.label: Comma after REMS clause
modes.description: A comma that closes an opening phrase about opioid risk programs, before the FDA or drug companies are named.
modes.example: and Drug Administration (FDA) has required a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) for these products. Under the requirements of the REMS<<,>> drug companies with approved opioid analgesic

modes.label: Start of sentence after disclaimer
modes.description: The first word of a sentence following a statement that uses are not proven.
modes.example: vesiculeux, vraic, wrack. These uses have been tested in humans or animals. Safety and effectiveness have not always been proven.<< Some>> of these conditions are potentially serious, and

card.writes: It lowers words like approved, allowed and permitted, so the next word is less likely to be a permission term.
card.plain: It fires at the pause after an opening phrase about FDA safety programs, just before the sentence names who must act.
